gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 9 build step is the narrowest honest place to widen runtime pilot coverage into the missing kretprobe lane.

A survey gate keeps the Linux anchor, the landed starter, diff, loader scaffold, and shared loader-request surfaces, plus the remaining broader runtime-control blocker, explicit while the pilot stays small.

A sample-backed lifecycle starter is the first honest runtime-facing kretprobe step that can model entry timestamps, return values, duration, and missed-instance bookkeeping without claiming loadable-module parity.
A dedicated Phase 9 test file keeps the starter reviewable and bounded around lifecycle transitions, symbol retargeting, and return-probe bookkeeping.
A narrow differential gate now captures a few entry-skip, duration, and nmissed expectations from the Linux sample before any broader runtime substrate work.

A bounded loader handoff makes the existing requires_runtime_substrate contract reviewable through explicit entry and exit symbol names, a no-substrate release path, and a kretprobe summary payload that now feeds the shared runtime-loader request surface.

The shared runtime-loader request surface now consumes the kretprobe loader handoff directly through `zigux/kernel/runtime_loader.zig`, keeping allocator posture, staged entry and exit symbols, and kretprobe payload facts machine-checkable before any real runtime execution path exists.

The kretprobe pilot still depends on the broader shared runtime-loader control surface tracked by the runtime loader gap survey: command-name, argv-policy, and environment-derived activation handling are still absent, so the pilot remains pre-execution.
